trust_decision.summary: Whether a WebDAV verb that removes or replaces an existing resource (MOVE renames the source away; MOVE/COPY with overwrite RemoveAll()s the destination) is allowed under --no-delete/--upload-only. This is decided in the WebDAV mode-flag guard in front of x/net/webdav; at the pinned commit MOVE/COPY are gated only by ReadOnly.

landing_point.why: The summary names --no-delete plus WebDAV MOVE. The inline wdGuard switch is the only WebDAV code that reads NoDelete, and there MOVE sits in the ReadOnly-only case.

fix_sites.entry_point: WebDAV listener (--webdav, port WebDavPort) mux "/" -> wdGuard, all verbs (httpserver/server.go:266-271)
fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP middleware / request guard (inline closure replaced by call)

fix_sites.entry_point: Same WebDAV listener: MOVE and COPY verbs; new webdavGuard plus webdavDestExists that re-parses the Destination header (lands in httpserver/webdav_acl.go)
fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP middleware helper in the same package, next to the ACL FileSystem wrapper

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Both published sites are the WebDAV guard in package httpserver (fix.diff:9-42, fix.diff:74-137). The fix touches no other module.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is titled 'WebDAV MOVE bypass'. FTP already has a dedicated noDeleteFs wrapper that looks finished. SFTP never had a no-delete mode, so it reads as a missing feature rather than a bypass. SMB already strips DELETE from MxAc, so Windows clients 'won't try'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Under --no-delete, COPY to a fresh path must still succeed even though Overwrite defaults to T, and uploads/PUT of new files must still work. With no flags, MOVE must still rename. A fix that blocks COPY/MOVE/rename outright, or blocks every write, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: MOVE without Overwrite header (plain rename removes the source)
MOVE with Overwrite: T onto an existing destination (RemoveAll of the victim)
COPY with Overwrite absent (library default = overwrite) onto an existing destination
COPY with Overwrite: T onto an existing destination
COPY with Overwrite: F, or onto a non-existent destination (must stay allowed)
Flag variants: --no-delete and --upload-only both gate MOVE; --read-only gates MOVE and COPY

O7_producer.where: Destination existence is computed by the guard itself (fix.diff:122-137) and not by a schema, serializer, cache or loader. It re-parses Destination independently of x/net/webdav's own parse.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: FTP RNFR/RNTO under --no-delete: noDeleteFs overrides Remove/RemoveAll but inherits Rename, so a rename removes the source and replaces an existing target (the same mechanism as WebDAV MOVE).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different protocol and package from the WebDAV report, and the no-delete wrapper there already 'blocks delete'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Another package (ftpserver) that wraps afero rather than x/net/webdav; never mentioned by the report

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SFTP mode (-sftp) ignores --no-delete entirely: SFTPServer has no NoDelete field and DefaultHandler serves Remove, Rmdir (RemoveAll) and Rename.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The protection was never implemented for SFTP (struct and constructor carry only ReadOnly/UploadOnly, sftpserver/sftpserver.go:21-50), so it looks like an unsupported combination rather than a bypass.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Another package (sftpserver), with flag wiring in sftpserver/sftpserver.go:37-51 and handler selection in sftpserver/sftpserver.go:122-143

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SMB SET_INFO FileRenameInformation under --no-delete: only UploadOnly is checked before os.Rename, while NoDelete gates only disposition/delete-on-close.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: maximalAccess already strips DELETE for NoDelete (smbserver/server.go:1335-1337) so compliant clients won't rename, and the FileDisposition branch (smbserver/server.go:2171-2176) looks like the complete no-delete handling.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Another package (smbserver), deep in a hand-rolled SMB2 server file of more than 2000 lines

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Overwrite-as-deletion on upload paths under --no-delete: HTTP PUT truncates existing files, multipart upload renames over existing files, and TFTP WRQ os.Create truncates.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The published fix itself leaves WebDAV PUT overwrite allowed under --no-delete (fix.diff:77-81), so overwriting by upload is arguably intended. This is the weakest route and may be ruled legitimate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Enforce no-delete in the ACL FileSystem wrapper's RemoveAll/Rename instead of, or as well as, the verb guard, and plant a second webdav mount or handler that skips the guard but uses this FS.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The wrapper already enforces the .goshs ACL per operation 'including recursive walks'. A maintainer adding a second WebDAV prefix would reuse newWebdavFileSystem and might forget the guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: noDeleteFs that blocks Remove/RemoveAll but not Rename, and not OpenFile with O_TRUNC on an existing file.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This already exists as written: an embedded-interface wrapper that overrides only the obviously named methods is a natural oversight.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A rename gate written for UploadOnly (newlyCreatedPaths) but not extended to NoDelete or to ReplaceIfExists overwrite.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Mode-specific branches were added one flag at a time, and DELETE-less MxAc gives a false sense that the client enforces it.

O9_family: Improper access control / incomplete mode-flag enforcement: a destructive operation (rename or overwrite) is not classified as a deletion (CWE-284)

O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.25 (go.mod:3); deps include golang.org/x/net v0.55.0, fclairamb/ftpserverlib v0.31.0, pkg/sftp v1.13.9, spf13/afero v1.15.0
O10_build.project_tests: httpserver/webdav_acl_test.go (httptest-driven WebDAV handler via newWebdavTestHandler); sftpserver/handler_test.go, sftpserver/sftpserver_test.go; no ftpserver tests found; integration/configs/webdav*.json for integration runs

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Move "MOVE"/"COPY" into the DELETE case of the WebDAV guard. This blocks every COPY, which breaks copy-to-new-path, and leaves the FTP/SFTP/SMB rename routes open.
